evidence: src/infrastructure/project-controller.ts: ProjectController.create inlines `const name = typeof body?.name === "string" ? body.name : ""` after casting `request.body as Record<string, unknown>`.

src/infrastructure/task-controller.ts: `private text(value: unknown): string { return typeof value === "string" ? value : ""; }`, plus inline `typeof body?.dueDate === "string" ? ... : undefined` and the same check for assigneeId.
src/infrastructure/user-controller.ts: `private stringField(body: unknown, field: string): string` adds a null/object guard on the body that the other two controllers do not have.
src/infrastructure/task-controller.ts: `if (status !== undefined && !isTaskStatus(status)) throw new ApplicationError("invalid task status", 400);` appears in both `create` and `list`.

src/infrastructure/in-memory-*-repository.ts and uuid-generator.ts implement the domain ports (ProjectRepository, TaskRepository, UserRepository, IdGenerator) consistently. That part of the module is cohesive.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module's overall concern holds together. It is the infrastructure adapter set: the HTTP controllers, the in-memory repositories that implement the domain repository ports, a UUID IdGenerator, and the composition root in http-server.ts and server.ts. The repositories and the ID generator use the domain ports consistently.

The HTTP request-parsing rule is not kept in one place, though. Every controller applies the same rule: a body or param field that is not a string becomes "" (or undefined when optional). Each controller implements it separately, and the three versions differ:
- ProjectController inlines it.
- TaskController has a private text() helper and also inlines typeof checks for dueDate and assigneeId.
- UserController has a private stringField() helper, which also guards against a null or non-object body.

The guard against an invalid task status is also written out twice inside TaskController (in create and in list), each time throwing ApplicationError("invalid task status", 400). This is an input-validation rule that should live in one shared helper for the HTTP adapter. It is copied with inconsistent behaviour, which matches the rubric's fail condition for duplicated rules. The duplication is small in scale, so confidence is moderate.

violations.message: The string-field coercion rule for request bodies is written inline in ProjectController.create instead of using one shared helper. The same rule is copied in TaskController.text and UserController.stringField, and the copies behave differently.

TaskController has its own private text() helper and inline typeof checks for the same coercion rule used by the other controllers. It also copies the 'invalid task status' 400 guard into both create and list.

UserController.stringField is a third, different implementation of the string-field coercion rule (it adds a null/object guard on the body). Request-body parsing therefore behaves differently from one controller to another.
